propertySets.notes: Any list of str including empty list and empty strings; small alphabet 'ab' produces frequent equal-length ties. Sandbox: 500/500 accepted.

propertySets.name: edge-cases

properties.name: empty_none
properties.description: None exactly when the list is empty.

properties.name: member_and_max_len
properties.description: Result is a string from the input and no input string is longer.

properties.name: first_of_ties
properties.description: Result is the earliest string with maximal length (strings before it are strictly shorter).
properties.code:
import copy
def prop_first_of_ties(candidate, strings):
    if strings:
        r = candidate(copy.deepcopy(strings))
        m = len(r)
        last = max(i for i, s in enumerate(strings) if len(s) == m)
        assert strings[last] == r

properties.name: append_not_longer
properties.description: Appending the result or a shorter string does not change the answer.

properties.name: append_longer_wins
properties.description: A strictly longer string wins wherever it is placed.
properties.code:
import copy
def prop_append_longer_wins(candidate, strings):
    base = max((len(s) for s in strings), default=0)
    new = 'z' * (base + 1)
    assert candidate(copy.deepcopy(strings) + [new]) == new
    assert candidate([new] + copy.deepcopy(strings)) == new

properties.name: prepend_tie_wins
properties.description: A same-length string prepended wins the tie; appended it loses.
properties.code:
import copy
def prop_prepend_tie_wins(candidate, strings):
    if strings:
        r = candidate(copy.deepcopy(strings))
        marker = '\x00' * len(r)
        assert candidate([marker] + copy.deepcopy(strings)) == marker
        assert candidate(copy.deepcopy(strings) + [marker]) == r

properties.name: reverse_same_length
properties.description: Reversing the list leaves the result length unchanged.

implementations.name: straightforward
implementations.notes: Strict > keeps the first of equal-length strings; None for empty list. Docstring examples passed.

implementations.name: brute-force
implementations.notes: Strict '>' keeps the first of equal-length strings; empty list returns None. Docstring examples pass in sandbox.

implementations.name: optimized
implementations.notes: max returns the first maximal element, matching the tie rule. Docstring examples passed in sandbox.

from typing import List, Optional


def longest(strings: List[str]) -> Optional[str]:
    """ Out of list of strings, return the longest one. Return the first one in case of multiple
    strings of the same length. Return None in case the input list is empty.
    >>> longest([])

    >>> longest(['a', 'b', 'c'])
    'a'
    >>> longest(['a', 'bb', 'ccc'])
    'ccc'
    """
